edges.effect_quant: In unaffected BRCA1 or BRCA2 carriers, prospective cohort evidence shows near-elimination of incident breast cancer after bilateral risk-reducing mastectomy over early and mid-term follow-up. The effect size is much larger than most cancer-screening or chemoprevention edges, even though the evidence base is observational rather than randomized.
edges.population: women with pathogenic BRCA1 or BRCA2 variants considering bilateral risk-reducing mastectomy before any breast-cancer diagnosis
edges.mechanism: Removing most at-risk breast tissue in BRCA carriers sharply reduces the tissue substrate available for future primary cancers, which is why the effect on incident breast-cancer risk is so large.
edges.summary: This is one of the strongest hereditary-risk-reduction incidence edges in the corpus. The evidence is observational and surgery is highly preference-sensitive, but across BRCA carrier cohorts the procedure consistently lowers incident breast cancer far more than surveillance alone.
edges.caveats: This edge is about cancer incidence reduction in unaffected BRCA carriers, not a recommendation for all high-risk women. The surgery has major reconstructive, sexual, and psychosocial consequences, and the evidence is not randomized because such trials are not realistically feasible.

evidence.citation: Meijers-Heijboer H et al 2001 N Engl J Med
evidence.notes: Breast cancer after prophylactic bilateral mastectomy in women with a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation.
